subject: Parallel defense & evidence handback — Order Form allocation proposal
messages:
From: Alex Torres <alex.t@nebulaapps.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redline — IP defense allocation request

Marissa / team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement and legal at NebulaApps reviewed the order form and attached a redline. Their primary outstanding asks are: (1) Redwood to accept defense control for third-party IP claims arising from customer use of the Service; (2) a clarified evidence and cooperation process with concrete SLAs; and (3) a cap carveout for willful infringement.

We understand Redwood has constraints around model provenance and third-party content. Can you confirm whether Redwood would consider a split: Redwood accepts defense for claims based on model code/weights and any infringing material introduced by Redwood-originated components, while NebulaApps would handle claims tied to customer-supplied content or their prompts? Also need a point-to-point evidence handback process and a named contact for litigation coordination.

I've attached the Nebula redline and an evidence checklist they want to add to the order form. Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Torres
Head of Procurement — NebulaApps

(415) 555-0198

Alex / Samantha,

Appreciate the clear asks and the redline; we've reviewed it internally. High level: we can be flexible on defense/control as long as allocation of responsibilities and evidence access is explicit and limited to claims that truly arise from Redwood-delivered artifacts (models, parameter updates, hosted assets). We cannot take open-ended responsibility for "customer prompt" content or third-party data the customer brings into the system.

Kimberly and Connor are looped to propose specific contract language and an operational playbook (who runs the defense, notice timing, privileged discovery handling, escrow trigger points). Rishi will advise on litigation-handling risk tolerance and insurance offsets.

Proposed next steps:
- Legal ops: Kimberly to send candidate redline language that narrows "customer indemnity" and defines evidence handback timeline.
- Ops: Connor to outline our evidence staging (what we can export: model hashes, request logs, KV caches) and expected data retention windows.
- Commercial: Marissa to propose a compromise on defense-control (parallel defense with defined handoff triggers).

Can we aim to close language by Friday so procurement has a final Order Form for signature next week?

-Marissa
Marissa Cole

Subject: Draft language + evidence process for Order Form (first pass)

Team / Alex & Samantha,

Attached is a first-pass redline snippet and an operational checklist. Key points of the proposal (keeps the customer comfortable while protecting Redwood's exposure):

1) Defense allocation: Redwood will defend and indemnify NebulaApps for third-party IP claims to the extent such claim arises from: (a) the original Redwood model code, parameter weights, or Redwood-hosted artifacts; or (b) model outputs proven, by forensic analysis, to be generated solely by Redwood-delivered components independent of customer-supplied content.

2) Customer responsibilities: NebulaApps will be responsible for claims that arise from customer-supplied data, prompts, or content it uploads or instructs the model to reproduce.

3) Parallel defense & cooperation: If both parties reasonably believe the claim implicates both buckets, parties will run a parallel defense with a lead counsel coordination call within 3 business days. Primary defense control remains with Redwood for Redwood-origin claims; if NebulaApps assumes control for its-origin claims, Redwood will provide all requested non-privileged evidence within 5 business days (see checklist).

4) Evidence checklist & retention: We listed the practical artifacts we can deliver (request logs, model version hash, KV cache exports for a specific user session, truncated prompt transcripts where retention permitted). We cannot export whole training corpora.

5) Escrow/insurance: For willful infringement findings, parties will follow the MSA insurance offset clause; we propose a carveout for willful acts proven by clear and convincing evidence.

Kimberly attached the redline and the "IP_evidence_checklist.xlsx" which enumerates the items and typical delivery times.

Open items we still need to resolve:
- How to treat derivative claims tied to third-party datasets used in model pretraining (legal is leaning to exclude).
- Specific DocuSign language for notice and discovery timelines (Connor to advise operations feasibility).

Alex / Samantha: does the parallel defense + 5 business day evidence delivery timeline work operationally on your side? If yes, we'll fold the language into the Order Form and send a final for signature.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Lead Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Kimberly / Marissa —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. The parallel-defense approach is promising and the 5-business-day evidence window seems workable. Two small asks from our GC: (1) add an explicit statement that Redwood will provide a named point of contact for evidence delivery and privileged counsel coordination; (2) add a short escalation path if Redwood cannot provide an item in the checklist (ie, 48-hour notice and a succinct reason with proposed remediation steps).

If you can add those two lines and circulate a final redline we can share with budgets & get signature authority queued. We appreciate the carveouts around pretraining datasets — that'll help our internal risk folks.

Samantha Lee
General Counsel — NebulaApps Inc.
